author: CatCutie_
body:
Age: 15

Timezone: GMT+2 (Central European Summer Time)

Do you have Teamspeak? yes

Do you have Discord? yes

Do you have access to a recording software? yes




CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION



Do you have any experience as a moderator on other servers?

No but zero used to be a moderator so I know the things I have to watch out for and what I have to do and what I cannot do.



What is your biggest weakness and how will it affect your moderating?

When I don’t agree with something I am usually quite vocal about it, I don’t believe it will affect my moderating too much though. I don’t type things in chat that shouldn’t be there (for example staff leaking wouldn’t happen) and if I don’t agree with something I also wouldn’t make a  post about it. I would either stay quiet or talk with another staff member to prevent staff leaking. The other way it would affect my moderating is that I would get frustrated and other mods would have to listen to me, but if it’s something that happens and it wouldn’t be staff leaking I am usually more vocal towards friends in chat or somewhere else when it regards something that isn’t about staff.

What qualities do you think a leader must have? Would you consider yourself a leader? Why/why not?
I think a leader should have the ability to help others in situations and push everyone to get better and not only help themselves. A leader should know what flaws there are and they should be able to fix them and not only know them, they should also know what people need and what they can do to provide their needs. I wouldn’t consider myself a leader since I am good at realizing what people need but bad at figuring out the way to help them get better at something. I’d rather stay in the background and help individuals instead of a whole group.



What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?

I’m quite strict in rules, I wouldn’t let anyone get away with breaking the rules, and if I don’t see it happen and someone else did I would always look at the evidence and if they broke the rules apply the correct punishment. I’m not very biased, even friends or people I know usually don’t break rules I wouldn’t let slip either because if you break the rules you should get punished. I know some people who would let punishments slip when it’s about friends and that’s why they wouldn’t want to become a moderator.



What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?

I think you should be able to just talk to them as friends, and if you don’t like them it shouldn’t affect the way you talk to them. If you really don’t like someone its best to just not say anything than try to be mean in chat. I do believe I have these skills, I am quite social and I wouldn’t say I don’t talk to people easily. If people ask me something or ask a moderator who is afk in chat when I am there and I know the answer I’m not afraid to answer that.



What in your opinion are the three main character traits a moderator must have when moderating?

I think selflessness, because you should be able to put other’s needs in front of your own(for example: Looking out for hackers when someone thought they saw one instead of playing)

I think a mod should be confident, to make mistakes and fix them instead of being insecure about them.

And most importantly I think a moderator should be intelligent. I think it speaks for itself that a mod shouldn’t just be blind and dumb about something.

 




CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS



You notice a moderator giving out a lot of false bans. They almost always have insufficient evidence or sometimes no evidence and they don’t seem to care. You notice it but other staff members don’t. What would you do?

I would alert a senior staff member or an admin about this issue, provide evidence along with my arguments and let them evaluate the situation. They have to take a decision on what to do on it since I can’t do more than that. I wouldn’t know what else to do since I have nothing more in my power to do about it.



You are in Teamspeak with a few other players and they begin talking quite disrespectfully about a particular staff member. You agree with what they’re saying to an extent, but the conversation starts to become racial and very disrespectful soon after. You are all in a nightclub channel where this is allowed. What would you do?

I would ask them to knock it off, maybe give a few of the good things the staff member does and if they don’t quit I would ask them again to talk about something else. Since I can’t do anything else than that that’s all I can ask from them.




You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confidential but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?

I would take a screenshot of what they said and send the evidence of staff leaking to a senior or admin, staff leaking is against the rules and it would be wrong of me to not notify it to another staff member. Even though its small I would rather not be biased about something small. Everything can be evaluated and I’m confident it’s the right thing to do. Rather have a staff member look at something small a few times than miss something big.




Some senior staff members are in teamspeak joking around with each other. They are removing others ranks, creating certain channels and even harassing certain users. They don’t mean any harm but some players in the channel feel a bit angry that they are using their permissions the way they are. What would you do?

I would record what was happening and send it to an admin or a higher staff member if they don’t knock it off. It’s for fun of course but abusing perks is also unfair, the higher staff members can decide what to do with it.




CRITERIA 3: OTHER

NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.




Why do you want to be a moderator?

I don’t really know to be honest, I’m just fascinated by helping people and I don’t think it’s wrong to start somewhere J I know a lot of people on avicus and helping them would be great as a moderator, not only as a friend.



What does Avicus mean to you?

Avicus is basically where my gaming life started. I started on minecraft, me and my friend found this server and we were not disappointed, 4 years later and we still play. Avicus means love to me, this is where I met zero obviously. It has a special place in my heart, besides all the toxicity that has made me consider leaving, I have also made friendships that would last forever.

Anything specific the staff team could do better?

The things I have noticed a lot is when someone has said something rude a few times or did something against the rules, the staff team doesn’t seem to notice it until I report even though it is quite obvious in my opinion.  But I don’t think that’s a big flaw, for the rest I think the staff team is doing great at the moment. Some people I never expected to become mods have become amazing mods.



Why did you choose to apply at Avicus?

Well this server is basically my home, I suck at pvp, I dislike the toxicity. But I love to be on avicus. If I would have to be moderator somewhere I would rather do it here than ANYWHERE else.



Do you have anything else to add to your application?

I really hope I get chosen, even if I fudge up everything else It would have been a great experience to know that I added a little value to the staff team. And If I don’t get chosen than that’s a lesson for next time! I would love to know what I could do better and what I do good if I get chosen/if I don’t.
